newsitem.title: PANAMA: Most Panamanians want U.S. to stay after 1999-poll.
newsitem.headline: Most Panamanians want U.S. to stay after 1999-poll.

text.p: Most Panamanians want U.S. troops to remain in Panama and the United States to continue running the Panama Canal after it is handed over on Dec. 31, 1999, according to a poll released Thursday.
According to a May survey of 1,200 Panamanians by international pollster Gallup, 54 percent do not believe Panama is adequately prepared to run the canal after the United States hands it over.
Some 74 percent also believe U.S. army bases should stay in Panama, and seven out of 10 favour a referendum on whether the Unites States should remain, a Gallup official told Reuters.
The poll, which had a 2.8 percent margin of error, was published a day after President Ernesto Perez Balladares signed legislation governing canal operations after the handover.
Balladares sought to reassure the international community Panama was ready to run the 51-mile (81 km) waterway, one of the world's most important.
The canal would be run as efficiently as, or more efficiently than, it was before the handover and would be administered by an independent authority, he said.
Under the 1977 Panama Canal Treaty, the United States is to cede operation of the canal and eight military bases to Panamanian control, and withdraw all U.S. troops.
